resources.string: Tools for checking your own exposure and getting intimate images taken down. Nothing here searches for other people, and nothing leaves your phone.
Have I Been Pwned lists data breaches your email address appeared in, including breaches of adult sites. Search only addresses you own.
StopNCII.org creates a digital fingerprint of an image on your own device. The image never leaves your phone, and participating platforms use the fingerprint to block matching copies.
Take It Down, from the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children, works the same way: a fingerprint is made on your device and the image itself is not uploaded.
Google lets you request removal of explicit or intimate images of you from its search results.
If someone is threatening you or you feel unsafe, contact your local law enforcement.
A self-audit you can work through at your own pace. Your checks are saved on this phone.
List every username you have used on social, gaming and forum accounts.
Search each username in quotes in a search engine and note anything you do not recognize.
Search your own email address at Have I Been Pwned and note any breaches.
Turn on breach notifications for your email addresses.
Change the password on any breached account, and anywhere you reused it.
Use a different password for every account, with a password manager.
Turn on two-factor authentication for your email and main accounts.
Close old accounts you no longer use.
Search your name in quotes and review the image results for anything you did not post.
Google Alerts emails you when a new web page mentions a username or name you choose. Set one for each of your own usernames.
Upload one of your own photos to Google Lens to see where copies of it appear online.
TinEye is another reverse image search and sometimes finds different matches than Google. Use it only with your own photos.
